events.label: Jeff Winston dies of heart attack 1988
events.description: Jeff Winston, a 43-year-old radio producer stuck in a failing marriage and a dead-end job, drops dead of a heart attack in 1988.

events.label: Wakes as 18-year-old in 1963 with full memories
events.description: Instead of dying, Jeff opens his eyes as his 18-year-old self in 1963, an Atlanta college student - with every memory of the forty-odd years to come still intact.

events.label: Replay for wealth via future knowledge
events.description: Armed with knowledge of the future, Jeff makes a fortune - betting on horse races and stock market rises he remembers - and lives the rich life he never had.

events.label: Always dies 1988; reboot with later start offset
events.description: No matter what Jeff changes, his heart gives out at the same age every time, and each death throws him back into his young body again - a little later each time.

events.label: Restart windows shorten each cycle
events.description: With every replay, the stretch of life Jeff gets to relive grows shorter, as if the universe is rationing out his second chances.

events.label: Notices film Starsea that never existed before
events.description: Jeff notices a film called Starsea that he has no memory of from his first life - proof that the world is subtly shifting under his changes.

events.label: Meets Pamela Phillips — fellow replayer
events.description: Jeff finds Pamela Phillips, a woman who calls the radio station knowing things she shouldn't - because she is a replayer too, reliving her own life with memories of the future.

events.label: Restart windows desynchronize between them
events.description: Jeff and Pamela's replays fall out of step - each returns to a different year and a different age - so even lovers separated by time itself cannot stay together.

events.label: Go public as oracles; government conscripts them
events.description: The two go public as oracles, predicting disasters and events, until the government steps in and takes control of their gift.

events.label: Imprisoned when geopolitics diverge
events.description: When their predictions start to change the future they remembered, their foreknowledge fails and the authorities hold them responsible, locking them away.

events.label: Loops shrink to repeatedly reliving original deaths
events.description: In the last replays, Jeff and Pamela find themselves forced to relive the very deaths that started it all, over and over, as the windows shrink to nothing.

events.label: Jeff survives 1988 heart attack; Pamela too
events.description: In the final cycle Jeff survives the 1988 heart attack - he simply lives on through it, and Pamela survives hers too, breaking the pattern at last.

events.label: Norwegian man wakes young in 1988 with memories to 2017
events.description: The book closes with an epilogue: a Norwegian man wakes young in 1988 carrying memories all the way to 2017, telling us the replays continue beyond Jeff's story.

events.label: Jeff dies 43; wakes 18
events.description: Jeff Winston dies at 43 and comes round as his 18-year-old self decades earlier, memories intact - the opening premise of the whole story.

events.label: Life replay with memory
events.description: Given his life to live again with full knowledge, Jeff gets to try out different ways of being alive each time round.

events.label: Different life strategies
events.description: Each replay Jeff plays the game differently - grabbing riches, seeking love, chasing meaning - and each strategy brings its own unexpected costs.

events.label: Meets other replayers
events.description: Jeff discovers he is not alone: other replayers are out there, most importantly Pamela, the woman who becomes his great love across lifetimes.

events.label: Power abuse temptations
events.description: The story keeps asking what a person would do with unlimited second chances - and watches Jeff and others flirt with using their foreknowledge selfishly and cruelly.

events.label: Replays end at death age
events.description: The replays always end at the same fateful age of death, with each cycle picking up a little further into Jeff's original life.

events.label: How to live a replay well
events.description: At its heart the book asks how to live a replayed life well - with love and openness rather than greed - and Jeff only learns it late.

events.label: Final acceptance
events.description: The story ends with acceptance: Jeff and Pamela stop fighting the pattern and simply live the life they have, together, while it lasts.

ruleEffects.effect: Exit ultimately requires surviving the terminal death, not gaming wealth
Other replayers share the phenomenon across overlapping windows

outcome.summary: Shortening life-replays end when Jeff and Pamela survive 1988; epilogue shows others still replaying.
